doll

In Nerve, Doll is given a body that can hold fears and desires it cannot experience for itself. In a doll story, a physical doll is photographed and shattered, and the images remain. The imagined vessel, the breakable object and the surviving photograph each offer a different way of encountering Doll. What kind of intimacy is possible with a figure that can be entrusted with things we find difficult to say and can never answer? Nerve · a doll story

Reading note. Alchemy and Jung. In Psychology and Alchemy, Jung proposes that an alchemist might unwittingly experience something from their own inner life as a quality of the material they are working with. Doll seems to hold feelings the speaker of Nerve finds hard to voice. Where do those feelings come from, and what happens to them when they are given a body? Psychology and Alchemy, §§345–347
